questions.q: Which component actually executes Java bytecode?
questions.explain: The JVM loads and executes bytecode; the JDK adds tools such as javac.

questions.q: What does javac produce from a .java file?
questions.explain: javac compiles source to platform-independent .class bytecode.

questions.q: Which signature is a valid entry point?
questions.explain: The launcher looks for public static void main with a String[] parameter.

questions.q: Java is best described as…
options: Compiled to bytecode, then JIT-compiled by the JVM
Purely interpreted like a shell script
Compiled directly to machine code by javac
questions.explain: Source compiles to bytecode, which the JVM interprets and JIT-compiles.

questions.q: What is the value of 7 / 2 in Java?
questions.explain: int / int is integer division; the fraction is discarded.

questions.q: Which type holds a single Unicode character?
questions.explain: char is a 16-bit unsigned primitive for one character.

questions.q: What does (int) 9.99 produce?
questions.explain: A narrowing cast to int truncates toward zero.

questions.q: Which declaration creates a constant?
questions.explain: final prevents reassignment; const is not a Java keyword.

questions.q: What does "java".substring(1, 3) return?
questions.explain: The end index is exclusive, so characters 1 and 2 are returned.

questions.q: Why does new String("java") == "java" evaluate to false?
options: == compares references and new String creates a distinct object
questions.explain: == compares references; equals compares content.

questions.q: Which is the mutable, non-synchronized string builder?
questions.explain: StringBuilder is mutable and unsynchronized; StringBuffer is synchronized.

questions.q: What does "  hi ".strip() return?
questions.explain: strip removes leading and trailing whitespace, including Unicode whitespace.

questions.q: What is printed by int x = 5; if (x > 3) System.out.print("A"); else System.out.print("B");
questions.explain: 5 > 3 is true, so the if branch runs.

questions.q: Which switch label avoids fall-through?
questions.explain: Arrow labels do not fall through; colon labels do unless you add break.

questions.q: What is the result of true && false || true?
questions.explain: && binds tighter: (true && false) || true is true.

questions.q: A switch expression over an enum must be…
questions.explain: Every enum constant must be covered, or a default supplied.

questions.q: How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) run?
questions.explain: i takes 0,1,2,3,4 — five iterations.

questions.q: What does continue do?
questions.explain: continue skips the rest of the body for the current iteration.

questions.q: Which loop always runs its body at least once?
questions.explain: do-while checks the condition after the body.

questions.q: What usually causes an infinite while loop?
options: The loop variable is never updated toward the exit condition
questions.explain: Without progress, the condition stays true forever.

questions.q: Which condition identifies a prime number n > 1?
options: n has more than two factors
questions.explain: Testing divisors up to sqrt(n) is sufficient and efficient.

questions.q: What is gcd(12, 18) using Euclid's algorithm?
What is missing if a recursive method throws StackOverflowError?
questions.explain: Without a base case the recursion never stops.

questions.q: Which value is an Armstrong number?
What is a valid overload of int add(int a, int b)?
questions.explain: Overloading needs a different parameter list, not just a different return type.

questions.q: What does a void method return?
questions.explain: void means no value is returned.

questions.q: Can a static method use this?
questions.explain: this refers to an instance, which a static context does not have.

questions.q: What is the signature of a method?
questions.explain: Return type and parameter names are not part of the signature.

questions.q: What is the last valid index of new int[5]?
questions.explain: Indices run from 0 to length - 1.

questions.q: How do you copy array contents?
options: Both Arrays.copyOf and clone copy contents
questions.explain: Arrays.copyOf and clone both create a new array with copied elements; plain assignment copies the reference.

questions.q: Which sort is stable and O(n log n) in the worst case for objects?
options: Quick sort with a fixed pivot
questions.explain: Arrays.sort for objects uses a stable TimSort.

questions.q: In a 2D array int[][] m = new int[3][4], what is m.length?
questions.explain: m.length is the number of rows.

questions.q: What runs when you write new Student()?
options: Nothing until a method is called
questions.explain: new allocates the object and invokes the matching constructor.

questions.q: Which access modifier hides a field from other classes?
questions.explain: private limits access to the declaring class.

questions.q: What does this refer to?
questions.explain: this is a reference to the instance whose method is running.

questions.q: Why prefer private fields with getters?
options: They preserve invariants and allow validation
questions.explain: Encapsulation keeps state valid and lets the representation change.

questions.q: Which call is resolved at runtime?
questions.explain: Dynamic dispatch selects the override based on the actual object type.

questions.q: What must a subclass constructor call when the parent has no no-arg constructor?
questions.explain: The subclass must invoke an existing parent constructor.

questions.q: Can a final method be overridden?
questions.explain: final prevents overriding.

questions.q: What does @Override do?
options: Makes a signature mismatch a compile error
questions.explain: The annotation is checked by the compiler.

questions.q: How many interfaces can a class implement?
questions.explain: Java allows multiple interface implementation.

questions.q: What is a functional interface?
options: An interface with exactly one abstract method
Any interface with a default method
questions.explain: One abstract method makes it a lambda target.

questions.q: When is an abstract class better than an interface?
options: When subclasses share state and partial implementation
When you need multiple inheritance of type
questions.explain: Abstract classes can hold fields and implemented methods.

questions.q: What does a default method allow?
options: Adding behaviour to an interface without breaking implementors
questions.explain: Default methods provide an implementation that implementors inherit.

questions.q: What does a record generate?
options: Constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString
questions.explain: Records generate the canonical members for their components.

questions.q: What does sealed permit?
options: Only listed types may extend or implement
questions.explain: Sealed restricts the subtype hierarchy.

questions.q: Which retention policy keeps an annotation available at runtime?
questions.explain: Reflection reads only RUNTIME annotations.

questions.q: What is an enum constant actually?
options: A public static final instance of the enum type
questions.explain: Each constant is a singleton instance of the enum.

questions.q: Which exception is checked?
questions.explain: IOException extends Exception but not RuntimeException.

questions.q: When does finally run?
questions.explain: finally runs whether or not an exception occurred.

questions.q: What should a catch block avoid?
questions.explain: Silent catches hide failures.

questions.q: What does try-with-resources require?
questions.explain: Declared resources must implement AutoCloseable.

questions.q: Which collection keeps keys sorted?
questions.explain: TreeMap orders keys by their natural order or a Comparator.

questions.q: What is the average lookup complexity of HashMap?
questions.explain: Hashing gives constant-time average lookup.

questions.q: Which Set preserves insertion order?
questions.explain: LinkedHashSet maintains insertion order.

questions.q: Which interface should you use for a FIFO queue?
questions.explain: Deque supports addLast/removeFirst queue operations.

questions.q: What does List<? extends Number> allow?
questions.explain: A extends wildcard is a producer: you can read but not add (except null).

questions.q: Why can't you create new T()?
options: Type erasure removes T at runtime
questions.explain: The runtime type parameter is erased.

questions.q: What happens when you unbox a null Integer?
questions.explain: intValue() on null throws NPE.

questions.q: Which is true about wrapper cache values?
questions.explain: Integer.valueOf caches the small range.

questions.q: Which class reads text efficiently line by line?
questions.explain: BufferedReader buffers characters and offers readLine.

questions.q: What does Files.readString do?
options: Reads the whole file into a String
questions.explain: It is a convenience method for small files.

questions.q: What is the risk of default Java serialization?
questions.explain: Serialized forms are brittle and unsafe for untrusted input.

questions.q: Which construct closes a file automatically?
questions.explain: try-with-resources calls close on AutoCloseable resources.

questions.q: Which is a terminal operation?
questions.explain: collect drives the pipeline and produces a result.

questions.q: What does map do?
questions.explain: map applies a function to each element.

questions.q: Why can't a stream be reused?
questions.explain: After a terminal operation the stream is consumed.

questions.q: What is the safe way to handle an absent Optional?
options: Null check on the Optional reference
questions.explain: orElse supplies a fallback instead of throwing.

questions.q: Which type makes an increment atomic?
questions.explain: AtomicInteger provides atomic read-modify-write operations.

questions.q: What does volatile guarantee?
options: Visibility and ordering for one variable
questions.explain: volatile does not make compound operations atomic.

questions.q: Why must an ExecutorService be shut down?
options: Pool threads are non-daemon and keep the JVM alive
questions.explain: Without shutdown the application may never exit.

questions.q: How do you prevent a lock-order deadlock?
options: Acquire locks in one global order
questions.explain: A consistent order removes the circular wait.

questions.q: Which JDBC type prevents SQL injection?
questions.explain: PreparedStatement binds parameters instead of concatenating SQL.

questions.q: What does a Connection transaction require?
options: A new DriverManager call per statement
questions.explain: Disabling auto-commit groups statements into one transaction.

questions.q: What is dependency injection?
options: Supplying collaborators from outside instead of constructing them inside
questions.explain: DI inverts control of object creation, improving testability.

questions.q: Which HTTP status means the request was invalid?
questions.explain: 400 Bad Request signals client-side validation failure.

questions.q: What does the JIT do?
options: Compiles hot bytecode to native code
questions.explain: The JIT profiles and optimises hot code paths.

questions.q: Which is a memory-leak cause in Java?
options: A static collection that never evicts
questions.explain: Unbounded reachable collections keep objects alive.

questions.q: Which pattern lets you swap algorithms at runtime?
questions.explain: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind an interface.

questions.q: What should a unit test avoid?
questions.explain: Unit tests isolate the unit under test with test doubles.
